# Simulator calibration against PRONOSTIA

**Generated by:** `python -m research.pronostia.calibrate --n-lifecycles 40`

PRONOSTIA: 17 run-to-failure bearings (9 with temperature). Simulator: 40 lives to bearing failure with only the bearing aging (noise_scale 0.5), matching the single-bearing PRONOSTIA rig.

Values are median [IQR] across trajectories. Curves are normalised health indicators over life fraction (0 = new, 1 = failure).

| Metric | PRONOSTIA (real) | Original simulator | Calibrated simulator |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vibration onset (life fraction where HI ≥ 0.2) | 0.96 [0.79, 0.98] | 0.24 [0.24, 0.25] | 0.96 [0.96, 0.96] |
| Vibration curve area (linear = 0.50) | 0.04 [0.02, 0.09] | 0.48 [0.48, 0.48] | 0.03 [0.03, 0.03] |
| Vibration failure/healthy ratio | 4.16 [3.14, 4.72] | 6.54 [6.51, 6.57] | 3.61 [3.59, 3.65] |
| Vibration curve RMSE vs PRONOSTIA median | 0 | 0.541 | 0.026 |
| Temperature rise to failure (°C) | 28.07 [17.77, 41.11] | 42.64 [42.37, 42.84] | 23.14 [22.97, 23.57] |
| Temperature curve area (linear = 0.50) | 0.79 [0.56, 0.96] | 0.48 [0.47, 0.48] | 0.71 [0.70, 0.72] |
| Temperature curve RMSE vs PRONOSTIA median | 0 | 0.320 | 0.103 |
| Lifetime coefficient of variation | 0.57 (all conditions pooled) | 0.00 | 0.52 |

## Fitted bearing law

`sensor = baseline + slope * g_k(bearing_wear)`, `g_k(w) = (exp(k w) - 1) / (exp(k) - 1)`

- Vibration shape k = **41.92** (applied to Vibration_X, Vibration_Y, Acoustic_dB)
- Temperature shape k = **-3.68** (Bearing_Temp)
- Slopes: Vibration_X +0.95, Vibration_Y +0.95, Acoustic_dB +15.00, Bearing_Temp +28.07
- Bearing lifetime lognormal sigma = 0.630 (pooled within-condition PRONOSTIA lifetimes)

## Caveats

- Units differ between PRONOSTIA (acceleration, g) and the simulator (velocity, mm/s); only dimensionless shape and failure/healthy ratio are calibrated.
- PRONOSTIA is an accelerated-degradation rig with a single bearing; the simulator's other five components (motor, oil seal, coolant seal, belt, spindle) have no counterpart and stay uncalibrated.
- PRONOSTIA temperature rises early in each test and then levels off (curve area > 0.5). Much of that early rise is likely the rig warming up rather than bearing wear, so read the fitted temperature shape with that in mind.
- A fitted k at the edge of the search range [-60, 120] means the real curve is steeper than g_k can express; the metrics table shows how close the calibrated curve still gets.
- The CNN-LSTM simulator checkpoint was trained on the ORIGINAL simulator. This script does not retrain it; retraining on the calibrated simulator is a separate step.
